draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Somanathapura! The Chennakeshava Temple here was consecrated in 1258 by a Hoysala general, and its walls, pillars and ceilings are covered in carvings.
draft.hungryLine: There aren't any very good restaurants here, so carry your own food.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Chennakeshava Temple is just a 3 min walk. Look for the Ramayana friezes on the south side and the Mahabharata on the north.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: The temple is fairly quiet, with no poojas held, so it's a calm place to sit and take in the carvings.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The temple stands on a high star-shaped platform with three sanctums for three forms of Vishnu, but the statue of Kesava in the western one is missing.

spots.name: Chennakeshava Temple
spots.detail: 3 min walk · A model of Hoysala architecture

legends.title: The stolen idol
legends.body: Locals say the main idol was stolen during one of the invasions because it was so beautiful. A replica stands in its place, so no poojas are held.

tips.title: Time your photos.
tips.body: Morning light is best on the front entrance, and evening light on the carved back side.

tips.title: Pack your lunch.
tips.body: There are no very good restaurants here, so bring food with you.

story.title: Hoysala lands
story.body: The Hoysala dynasty ruled this area, and a minister named Somanatha planned a temple here on the bank of the Kaveri.

story.title: The temple is consecrated
story.body: Somanatha Dandanayaka, a general of King Narasimha III, consecrated the Chennakeshava Temple in 1258.

story.title: Invasions
story.body: The temple suffered several invasions, and during one of them the main idol is said to have been stolen.

story.title: World heritage
story.body: The temple was recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.
